chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymoun, from Ma'mar ibn Umar, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the sick person: does he make up the prayer if he was unconscious? He (peace be upon him) said: No.

key_terms.يَقْضِي: he makes up / fulfills the lapse

ai.seo_question: Does a sick person need to make up missed prayers if they were unconscious during the prayer times?
ai.summary: In this foundational narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies that unconsciousness (*ghafla*) acts as a complete exemption from the obligation of making up missed prayers (*qada*), distinguishing it from mere forgetfulness or sleep. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the *taklif* (obligation) is suspended when the faculty of consciousness is entirely lost, a key distinction in the *Fiqh* of *Salat*. The chain of transmission highlights the reliability of the Kufan scholars, such as Thalaba ibn Maymun, in preserving these precise legal nuances regarding the sick.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hajjal, from Sa’alba Bin Maymoun, from Ma’mar Bin Umar who said,
‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about the sick one, Does he have to fulfil the lapse Salāts when he was unconscious?’ Heasws said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hajjal from Tha’labah ibn Maymun from Ma‘mar ibn ‘Umar who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about one suffering from illness if one is required to perform one’s Salah (prayer) again which is missed during the time of fainting condition. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, one is not required to perform such Salah (prayer) again.’”
